critical_code_review_comments: SESSION 125 FIXES ARE CORRECT AND MINIMAL: The two new resolver helpers (_resolve_marker_url, _resolve_subject_crop_url) mirror the exact pattern of the existing _resolve_video_url / _resolve_poster_url — override wins, fallback to /api/uploads/{filename}. Symmetry preserved.

R2 FLUSH IS IDEMPOTENT AND SAFE: The marker/subject_crop R2 upload blocks (L5136-5159) both check `if not doc.get('..._url_override')` before uploading, so replaying the flush on an already-flushed report is a no-op. Correct.

LOCAL FILE PRESERVATION FOR MARKER: L5145 comment explicitly notes that the local marker JPEG is NOT deleted after R2 upload — kept for admin re-runs since it's tiny (~50 KB). Video and poster ARE unlinked after R2 flush because they can be re-derived from the video. Sensible tradeoff.

FRONTEND UNLOCK LOGIC IS CENTRALIZED: ReportPage.jsx L1910-1911 computes unlocked ONCE per render and uses it 15+ times below. Any future role added to the premium tier just needs to be added to the whitelist in this one line. No scattered role checks. Same clean pattern in UploadPage.jsx L20.

TIMER FIX IS TRUE CLIENT-SIDE (correct scope): hideTimers is a pure UI hint — the backend still runs the same timers and still returns wall-clock progress. Only the label is swapped. This is the right layer to make the change since premium users' upload processing isn't actually different from free users' upload processing (both run through the same analyze_preview_task pipeline).

MINOR OBSERVATION (non-blocking): The backend now exposes subject_crop_url in both /reports/{id} and /reports/{id}/status, but ReportPage.jsx does not consume it — the 'Zoomed crop' UI is rendered by CSS-cropping the marker JPEG client-side (a canvas ~200x200 zoom of the marker's bbox). This is fine for now, but if the marker frame is ever cropped to a different aspect than the subject bbox, the client-side crop math will drift out of sync. A future improvement would be to switch the 'Zoomed crop' to `${ASSET_BASE}${subject_crop_url}` when present, and only fall back to CSS cropping when subject_crop_url is null (legacy reports).
MINOR (carried from prior sessions): server.py is now 11,176 lines. The 4 URL resolvers (video/poster/marker/subject_crop) are ~15 lines each and could live together in a util module. Not blocking.

rca of the issue: PROBLEM: (1) 'Your Player · Tracked' image showed a white box/[?] placeholder on the report page. (2) Admin/premium users saw the blurred+locked preview instead of the full report. (3) Wall-clock 'Elapsed · MM:SS' timer was shown to paid users during analysis (leaked their wait time). ROOT CAUSES: (1) The marker.jpg + subject_crop.jpg were only written to the pod's local /uploads directory during analyze_preview_task; on pod rollover the ephemeral disk was wiped, so /api/uploads/{filename} → 404. The DB still pointed at the legacy filename via marker_filename with no R2 override. Only video.mp4 and poster.jpg were being flushed to R2. (2) ReportPage.jsx's `unlocked = is_paid || manually_unlocked` did not include the user's role, so even admins hit the paywall UI. (3) UploadPage.jsx passed no hideTimers prop to PrecisionScanOverlay, and the overlay unconditionally rendered `Elapsed · MM:SS`. FIXES: (1) Added marker + subject_crop R2 upload blocks inside _flush_preview_artifacts_to_r2 (server.py L5136-5159), added _resolve_marker_url + _resolve_subject_crop_url helpers (L4559, L4574) that prefer the R2 override over the legacy path, and wired them into /reports/{id} + /reports/{id}/status + _serialize_report. Ran /app/backend/tests/backfill_r2_marker.py against 25 legacy reports to flush their local JPEGs to R2. (2) Added premiumRole=['admin','premium','vip','scout'].includes(user?.role) to ReportPage.jsx L1910, then unlocked = is_paid || manually_unlocked || premiumRole. (3) Added isPaidTier constant to UploadPage.jsx L20 using same role whitelist, passed as hideTimers to PrecisionScanOverlay L473, which renders 'Working in the background' when true and `Elapsed · MM:SS` when false. All 3 fixes verified live via 17/17 pytest + browser E2E.
